court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
trial_court: Principal District Court at Tiruvallur, GWOP No.363 of 2021
facts_of_case: The parties were married in 2009 and have two male children. The respondent filed O.P.No.1697 of 2021 for dissolution of marriage in the V Additional Family Court, Chennai. The petitioner seeks to transfer GWOP No.363 of 2021 from Tiruvallur to Chennai.

legal_principles.principle: The domicile or citizenship of the opposite party is immaterial in a case like this.
legal_principles.held: In case the marriage was solemnized under Hindu Law marital relationship is governed by the provisions of the Hindu Marriage Act. Therefore, Section 19 has to be given a purposeful interpretation.

legal_principles.principle: The residence of the wife determines the question of jurisdiction.
legal_principles.held: It is the residence of the wife, which determines the question of jurisdiction, in case the proceeding was initiated at the instance of the wife.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the court to give a meaningful interpretation to beneficial provisions.
legal_principles.held: Therefore such a beneficial provision meant for the women of our Country should be given a meaningful interpretation by Courts.

legal_principles.principle: The place of residence of the wife is a relevant factor in transfer petitions.
legal_principles.held: In the case of Mona Aresh Goel vs. Aresh Satya Goel [(2000) 9 SCC 255], when the wife pleaded that she was unable to bear the traveling expenses and even to travel alone and stay at Bombay, the Supreme Court ordered transfer of proceedings.
cited_cases: Mona Aresh Goel vs. Aresh Satya Goel [(2000) 9 SCC 255]

legal_principles.principle: The court should consider the difficulties faced by the wife in traveling to contest proceedings.
legal_principles.held: In the case of Lalita A.Ranga vs. Ajay Champalal Ranga [(2000) 9 SCC 355], the wife has filed a petition to transfer the proceedings initiated by the husband for divorce, at Bombay. The place of residence of the wife was at Jaipur, Rajasthan.
cited_cases: Lalita A.Ranga vs. Ajay Champalal Ranga [(2000) 9 SCC 355]

outcome.final_order: The petition for transfer is allowed and GWOP No.363 of 2021 will be transferred to the V Additional Family Court, Chennai.
